CHAPTER I 
RECOMMENDATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE GOVERNMENT 
OVERALL ASSESSMENT OF THE DEMANDS FOR GRANTS (2025-26) OF THE MINISTRY 
OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT (M/o WCD) 
 
Recommendation 
The Committee observes that Ministry has been allocated Rs. 26,889.69 crores under BE 2025-26 
which is 0.53% of the total budget allocation of the Government of India. Further, allocation at BE 
2025-26 is 3.05% more than BE 2024-25 and 15.98% more than RE 2024-25. The Committee notes that 
Ministry of Women and Child Development caters to 67% population of the country as per the Census 
2011, however, allocation of only 0.53% of the total budget allocation for FY 2025-26, is very meagre 
amount to facilitate implementation of various schemes and plans. The Committee, therefore, 
recommends the Ministry to seek more funds from Ministry of Finance at the RE stage so that the 
schemes/plans do not shift due to shortage of funds.      
                      (Para 2.4 ibid) 
 
Reply 
The Ministry acknowledges the observations of the Committee regarding the budgetary allocation for 
the financial year 2025–26 and submits that it is committed for effective implementation of its schemes 
and programmes.  However, it may be appreciated that Ministry of WCD is one of the several 
Ministries which are involved in the area of work related to development of women and children.   
Health, Education, Rural Development, Food and Public Distribution, Social Justice and Empowerment, 
Tribal Affairs, Agriculture, etc., are other key Ministries which are involved in this job.  Moreover, the 
expenditure in this Ministry is demand driven and the budget of the Ministry is fixed taking this into 
account.  However, the Ministry will approach Ministry of Finance at the suitable stage for enhancing 
the allocations so that the schemes are not affected due to financial constraints. 
 
Recommendation 
The Committee notes that Ministry was allocated Rs. 26,092.19 crores at BE 2024- 25 which was 
reduced by 11.14% to Rs. 23,182.98 crores at RE 2024-25, which is Rs. 1835.48 crores less than the 
Actual utilization by the Ministry during 2023-24. Moreover, the Actual utilization during 2024-25 as 
on 17.02.2025 is only 18,497.21 crores which is 70.89% of BE 2024-25 and 79.79% of the RE 2024-
25.The Committee feels that in view of the inflationary trends in the country, the allocation and Actual 
utilization should increase at least 8% to 10% over the allocation/utilization during previous year to 
accommodate the inflation and to maintain the existing standards for expenditure by Ministry and to 
avoid further decline in actual allocation/expenditure. Further, the Ministry of Finance should be taken 
into confidence so that substantial reduction in allocations at RE stage is avoided in order to make the 
schemes efficacious.           
(Para 2.5 ibid) 
Reply 
The Ministry takes note of the Committee’s observations regarding the reduction in allocation at the 
Revised Estimates (RE) stage. All out efforts were made by the Ministry to enhance the allocation. 
Consequently, MoF allocated an additional fund of Rs.1405.32 crore in RE 2024-25 due to which total 
RE became to Rs.24588.30 crore against which an amount of Rs.24529.48 crore was incurred by the 
Ministry i.e 99.76% of Final RE.  Further, the Ministry will also engage proactively with the Ministry 
of Finance to avoid substantial reductions at the RE stage in future and seek adequate funds in 
alignment with schemes' requirements and inflation-adjusted needs.  Efforts will be made to get 
sufficient budget outlay for the schemes of the Ministry during the forthcoming 16th Finance 
Commission. 
 
Recommendation 
The Committee notes that Actual utilization by the Ministry over allocation at RE and BE had been 
89.22% and 62.47%, respectively during 2020-21, 91.73% and 87.10%, respectively during 2021-22, 
98.32% and 93.40%, respectively during 2022-23 and 98.31% and 98.31% during 2023-24. However, 
Actual utilization as on 17th February, 2025 over RE and BE 2024-25 has been 79.79% and 70.89%, 
respectively. In this regard, the Committee would like to refer to Rule 56(3) of General Financial Rules 

3 
 
(GFR), which states that rush to expenditure particularly in the closing months of financial year should 
be avoided in future. As per the guidelines, the last quarter expenditure must be limited to actual 
procurement of goods and services and reimbursement of expenditure already occurred. Ministry of 
Finance's instructions seeks to restrict last quarter expenditure to 33% ceiling and last month (March) 
expenditure to 15% ceiling only.  
In backdrop of the Actual Expenditure by Ministry of Women and Child Development during 2024-25 
and Rule 56(3) of General Financial Rules (GFR), the Committee recommends that the Ministry should 
adhere to Rule 56(3) of GFR, streamline its expenditure during 2025-26 to optimize the utilization of 
funds allocated to it and to avoid piling up of expenditure in the last quarter of the financial year. 
          (Para 2.6 ibid) 
Reply 
During the F.Y 2024-25, an amount of Rs.26092.19 crore was allocated by Ministry of Finance which 
was reduced to Rs.23182.98 crore at RE stage. An amount of Rs.3308.20 crore was sought from 
Ministry of Finance during 2nd Supplementary Demands however, at that time funds were not 
provided.  However, keeping in view good expenditure trend and further efforts made by the Ministry, 
an additional amount of Rs.1405.32 crore was allocated by MoF during the last month of Financial 
Year.  Accordingly, final RE of the Ministry was enhanced to Rs.24588.30 crore against which an 
amount of Rs24529.48 crore was incurred by the Ministry i.e. 99.76% of Final RE 2024-25 and 94.01% 
of BE 2024-25. It is also to be mentioned that necessary relaxation was obtained from MoF for 
incurring more than 33% and 15% of Budget Estimates during last quarter and last month respectively. 
However, it is stated that necessary measures will be undertaken during F.Y 2025-26 onwards to 
streamline the planning and execution of schemes and programmes to avoid any such rush of 
expenditure in the last quarter. 
  
Recommendation 
From perusal of Table 3 & 4, it is evident that there are huge variations of allocations such as (-) 
45.63% under Anganwadi Services, (-)23.44 under Mission Vatsalya earlier Child Protection Services, 
(-)33.33 under Nari Adalat, (-)28.83% under Shakti Sadan and Home for Widows earlier Swadhar 
Greeh/Ujjawala, (-)16.67% under Palna/ National Creche Scheme and (-)31.82% under Gender 
Budgeting in BE 2025-26 over projections made by the Ministry of Women and Child Development to 
Ministry of Finance. Further, there are huge variations of (-) 35.71% under National Institute of Public 
Cooperation and Child Development NIPCCD/SPNIWCD, (-) 26.44% under National Commission for 
Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) and (-) 11.70% under National Commission for Women over 
projections made by the Ministry to Ministry of Finance. Similarly, there is overall variation of (-) 
40.37% and (-) 25.58% in scheme-wise and Organization/ Institution/Bodies-wise in BE 2025-26, 
respectively over projections made by the Ministry to Ministry of Finance. The Committee, therefore, 
recommends that review of the Projections made to Ministry of Finance and actual allocations made in 
respect of each scheme should be undertaken by the Ministry of Women and Child Development 
wherein there is gap between projections and allocations to make implementation of schemes/plans 
more realistic. The Committee also recommends the Ministry to monitor the physical and financial 
progress of the schemes, so that these schemes do not suffer due to reduced allocations. Such an 
objective review will help the Ministry to seek additional funds at RE stage for the schemes/plans.  
The Committee further recommends the Ministry of Finance to allocate funds to the Ministry of 
Women and Child Development liberally against the projections in view of the fact that the Ministry 
caters more than half of the population of the country and runs many crucial schemes for their well-
being and development. 
          (Para 2.8 ibid) 
Reply 
The Ministry of Women and Child Development acknowledge the recommendations of the Committee. 
The Ministry has reviewed the projections made to the Ministry of Finance and the actual allocations 
received under each scheme. This exercise will aid in aligning future projections with realistic 
implementation needs. Further, the Ministry is also making efforts to strengthen its monitoring 
mechanisms to track both physical and financial progress of schemes to ensure their effective 
implementation of the schemes. 
Further, it is mentioned that significant gap between projection made by this Ministry to MoF 
and actual allocation of fund provided to this Ministry by MoF is mainly under the scheme Saksham 

4 
 
Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 as MoF provided the fund under this scheme considering the total outlay 
approved for this scheme during the 15th Finance Commission. However, efforts are being made by the 
Ministry to get the outlay of the scheme increased during 2025-26 with the approval of the Competent 
Authority. 
 Further, as regards to cut imposed by MoF in other schemes, it was due to availability of 
unspent balance in SNA accounts with States/UTs.  To resolve this issue, regular VCs are being made 
and regular advisories to the states are also being issued. The Ministry is hopeful that the measures 
being taken will reduce the unspent balance with the states significantly resulting in expenditure of fund 
as per approved Quarterly Expenditure Plan.   
Variation in projection made by the Ministry and allocation by MoF in respect of 
NIPCCD/SPNIWCD, NCPCR and NCW was due to the fact that distribution of fund in Autonomous 
Bodies and Secretariat was to be done within available fund under non-scheme.  However, efforts will 
be made get more fund for the aforesaid Bodies during RE or supplementary grant stage. 
 
Recommendation 
The Committee observes that the Ministry acts as the nodal Ministry which runs important programmes 
like Saksham Anganwadi, Poshan 2.0 for children, Mission Vatsalya and Mission Shakti for the 
development of women and children and many of the programmes run by the Ministry play a 
complementary role to developmental programmes in the sectors of health, education, rural 
development, and safety of women and children. However, the Committee notes that the total unutilized 
funds with respect to BE 2023-24 is Rs. 1622.32 crores while it is Rs. 804.21 crores with respect to RE 
2023-24 under Mission Shakti against allocation of Rs. 3143.96 crores and Rs. 2325.85 crores at BE 
and RE 2023-24, respectively. The total unutilized fund during 2023-24 under 
 
SAMARTHYA Scheme is Rs. 1416.83 crores and Rs. 698.72 crores against BE & RE 
allocations of Rs. 2581.96 crores and Rs. 1863.85 crores, respectively which is not satisfactory. 
Similarly, the total unutilized fund during 2023-24 under SAMBAL Scheme is Rs. 205.49 crores and Rs. 
105.49 crores against BE & RE allocations of Rs. 562.00 crores and Rs. 462.00 crores, respectively 
which is also not very satisfactory.         
(Para 2.11 ibid) 
Reply 
Ministry acknowledges the observation made by the Committee. Further, it is stated that the less 
expenditure was incurred in Mission Shakti scheme during the FY 2023-24 mainly due to incomplete 
proposal received from the States and unspent balance lying in the SNA account of the States under the 
various components of sub schemes of Sambal and Samarthya under Mission Shakti. In so far as 
PMMVY which is the largest constituent of Samarthya sub-scheme, is concerned, the major reasons for 
the funds not being released to several States/UTs were the non-compliance of mandatory SNA norms 
(formulated by Department of Expenditure) by those States, regarding requirement of deposit of Central 
share of Interest accrued in the bank account, deficit in the transfer of funds from State Treasury to 
SNA bank accounts of the respective schemes, etc. Under PMMVY, the transition to new software 
which is Paper-less and Aadhaar authentication and NPCI seeding enabling, also led to slow 
implementation by the States/ UTs. The transition to new software is now complete (except in cases of 
Tamil Nadu and Odisha, where the scheme is being implemented in co- branded manner with the 
corresponding state schemes). Accordingly, the fund release and utilization should now improve 
significantly. Also, the pending applications from the old software have now been migrated into the 
new software through a separate module. As a result, the process of payment to beneficiaries should 
now be expedited. 
Recommendation 
The Committee further observes that during 2024-25, the unutilized funds as on 31st January, 2025 
under Saksham Anganwadi and POSHAN 2.0 with respect to BE and RE is Rs. 5661.17 crores and Rs. 
4532.07 crores against BE and RE allocations of Rs. 21200.00 crores and Rs. 20070.90 crores, 
respectively. Under Mission Vatsalya, unutilized funds as on 31st January, 2025, with respect to BE 
and RE are Rs. 568.80 crores and Rs. 487.63 crores against BE and RE 2024-25 allocations of 
Rs.1472.17 crores and Rs. 1391.00 crores, respectively. Under SAMBAL scheme unutilized funds as on 
31st January, 2025, with respect to BE and RE are Rs. 472.58 crores and Rs. 265.94 crores against BE 
and RE 2024-25 allocations of Rs. 629.00 crores and Rs. 422.36 crores, respectively. Under 

5 
 
SAMARTHYA scheme unutilized funds as on 31st January, 2025, with respect to BE and RE are Rs. 
1823.28 crores and Rs. 335.05 crores against BE and RE 2024-25 of Rs.2516.97 crores and Rs. 
1028.74 crores, respectively. Under Mission Shakti unutilized funds as on 31st January, 2025, with 
respect to BE and RE are Rs. 2295.86 crores and Rs. 600.99 crores against BE and RE 2024-25 of 
Rs.3145.97 crores and Rs. 1451.10 crores, respectively.  
The Committee notes that increased BE is allocated which is reduced at RE stage in general, 
and up to 30-40% in case of schemes like Mission Shakti in particular. The Actual utilization is again 
very less vis-à-vis BE and RE allocations during 2023-24 and 2024-25. The Committee therefore, 
recommends that the Ministry should adhere to Rule 56(3) of GFR and streamline its expenditure 
during 2025-26 to optimize the utilization of funds allocated to it and to avoid piling up of expenditure 
in the last quarter of the financial year. Further, trend of substantial reduction in allocations at RE 
stage under various schemes of the Ministry should be taken care of and avoided as far as possible. 
          (Para 2.12 ibid) 
Reply 
This Ministry acknowledges the recommendation made by the Committee. Further, it is to mention that 
during the F.Y 2024-25, an amount of Rs.26092.19 crore was allocated by MoF which was reduced to 
Rs.23182.98 crore at RE stage. But with the efforts made by the Ministry, an additional amount of 
Rs.1405.32 crore was allocated by MoF under all three Missions of this Ministry due to which Final RE 
came to Rs.24588.30 crore against which an amount of Rs.24529.48 crore was incurred by the Ministry 
i.e. 99.76% of Final RE 2024-25 and 94.01% of BE 2024-25. 
Moreover, it is also stated that the schemes viz Mission Vatsalya, Mission Shakti and Saksham 
Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 are mostly demand driven schemes and the release of funds also depends on 
receipt of the proposals complete in all respects, as per the schematic norms and duly recommended by 
the State Governments/UTs. Sometimes the proposals are received at the fag end of the FY resulting in 
more release during the last quarter of FY.  However, it is stated that necessary measures will be 
undertaken during F.Y 2025-26 to streamline the planning and execution of schemes and programmes 
to avoid any rush of expenditure in the last quarter. 
 
Recommendation 
The Committee notes that the unspent balances in States’ SNA accounts are substantial and that they 
are part of the reason the Ministry is unable to secure a larger budget. The Committee was provided 
state-wise details of the same, which are attached in Annexure 1. The Committee recommends that the 
Department work more closely with State Governments to understand the constraints, if any, in 
spending the outstanding SNA balance and the steps that can be undertaken to accelerate the utilization 
of these funds.     
(Para 2.13 ibid) 
Reply 
For resolving the issue of SNA balance, regular follow up meetings, both physical and through VCs, are 
being held with the States /UTs since last 2 years.  The Ministry is hopeful that with the regular efforts 
being made, the availability of unspent balance with the states will reduce significantly.  Here, it is also 
stated that with the Mission Shakti scheme of the Ministry getting onboarded on SNA SPARSH module 
from SNA module, the issue of unspent balance will not be there and expenditure will be made on real 
time basis. 
 
SCHEMES/MISSIONS OF THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN & CHILD DEVELOPMENT 
 
Recommendation 
The Committee notes that the Ministry was allocated for Centrally Sponsored Schemes like Saksham 
Anganwadi and POSHAN 2.0, Mission Vatsalya, Mission SHAKTI and Other Schemes Funded from 
Nirbhaya Fund, a total of Rs. 25848.14 crores under BE 2024-25 which was reduced to Rs. 22943.00 
crores at RE stage. Out of the said allocation Ministry has been able to spend Rs. 18,284.24 crores only 
as on 17th February, 2025 under these flagship schemes which pegs at 70.73% & 79.69% of the BE & 
RE 2024-25, respectively. The Committee expresses its concern over the poor fiscal management and 
under utilization of allocated funds under various flagship schemes of the Ministry like Saksham 
Anganwadi and POSHAN 2.0, Mission Vatsalya, Mission SHAKTI and Other Schemes Funded from

  Anganwadi Workers (AWWs) and Anganwadi Helpers (AWHs) are “honorary workers” from

development to help the community. Being honorary and voluntary workers, they are paid a monthly

opportunities for Anganwadi Workers have been enhanced. 50% posts of Anganwadi Workers shall be 
filled by promotion of Anganwadi Helpers and 50% posts of Supervisors shall be filled by promotion of 
Anganwadi Workers subject to fulfilment of other criteria. States/ UTs have been requested to adopt a 
uniform retirement date i.e 30th April of each year with respect to Anganwadi Workers and Helpers to 
ensure proper human resource planning.

provided to Anganwadi Workers and Helpers under Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana 
(PMJJBY) for life cover of Rs.2.00 lakh (covers life risk, death due to any reason) to AWWs/AWHs in 
the age group of 18 to 50 years and Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana for accidental cover of

disability) to AWWs and AWHs in the age group of 18-59 years. Insurance cover under PMJJBY and 
PMSBY is provided to AWWs/AWHs through their bank accounts and the funds towards premium

Scheme.

  The introduction of Poshan Tracker has significantly streamlined the operations of AWWs, 
reducing the time-consuming and cumbersome tasks they previously undertook. Prior to Poshan 
Tracker, AWWs were burdened with maintaining physical records of growth monitoring, carrying 
bulky IEC materials, manually scheduling home visits and updating 9 registers on regular basis. The

is available every month. Aadharshila "ECCE-Learning" module has also been incorporated in Poshan 
Tracker Application which provides daily learning prompts in the form of videos and voice notes for all 
Anganwadi Workers (AWWs). 
Poshan Tracker application and dashboard has not only eliminated the need to keep physical 
registers, it has reduced drudgery from the daily work routine of the AWW and has increased her 
capacity for more direct engagement with beneficiaries and quality improvement in service delivery

The Committee notes that the PMMVY is currently only available to all woman aged 18-55 years for 
their first child, and to women who have a second child only if the child is a girl. The Committee was 
informed that the PMMVY Rules, 2022 were notified under sub-section 3 of section 39 of the National 
Food Security Act, 2013 on 22nd December, 2022. The NFSA says that “every pregnant woman and 
lactating mother shall be entitled to…maternity benefit of not less than rupees six thousand, in such 
instalments as may be prescribed by the Central Government.” The Act is therefore unequivocal that 
the maternity benefit is due to every pregnant woman and not only to those pregnant with their first 
child and/or second girl child. The Committee recommends that the Department extend the benefits 
provided under PMMVY to all eligible pregnant and lactating women, not just those with their first 
child and/or a second a girl child, particularly of women from BPL families.

6,000 whereas the amount due under PMMVY is only Rs 5,000. The Committee was informed by the 
Department that eligible women may be receiving another Rs 1,000 through the JSY after institutional 
delivery, which would bring the composite amount to Rs. 6,000. The Committee notes that the NFSA 
was brought with the intention to ensure food security for pregnant and lactating women, and that it 
must not be linked to the JSY which is focused on institutionalization of childbirth. Hence, the PMMVY 
amount must be increased to Rs. 6,000. Further, periodic increase in the PMMVY amount must be 
undertaken, indexed to food price inflation.

Reply 
The National Food Security Act, 2013 (NFSA) provides that subject to such schemes as may be framed 
by the Central Government, every Pregnant Women & Lactating Mother (PW&LM), except those who 
are in regular employment with the Central Government or State Government or Public Sector 
Undertaking or those who are in receipt of similar benefits under any law for the time being in force, 
shall be entitled to maternity benefit of not less than rupees six thousand, in such instalments as may be 
prescribed by the Central Government.

Under Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY), maternal benefit of ₹5,000/- is 
provided to eligible Pregnant Women & lactating Mothers (PW&LM) during the period of pregnancy 
and lactation. The eligible beneficiary also receives the remaining cash incentive as per approved norms 
towards maternity benefit under Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) after institutional delivery so that on an 
average, a woman gets ₹6,000/-. 
Normally, the first pregnancy of a woman exposes her to new kinds of challenges and stress 
factors. Hence, the scheme provides support to the mother for safe delivery and immunization of her 
first child. Under Mission Shakti, w.e.f. 01.04.2022, to promote positive behavioural change towards 
girl child, the maternity benefits of ₹6000 is also provided to beneficiaries for second child subject to 
condition that the second child is a girl. 
Every pregnant women & lactating mother is entitled to meal, free of charge, during pregnancy 
and six months after child birth through the Anganwadi, so as to meet the nutritional standards specified 
in schedule of NFSA Act. These foodgrains are being allocated to the states through the Wheat Based 
Nutritional Programme (WBNP) wherein foodgrains (Wheat/Rice/Coarse grains (Millets)) are allocated 
to the States/UTs through the Department of Food & Public Distribution for use as Supplementary 
Nutrition at NFSA rates.However, the suggestion of the Committee has been noted for further 
consideration.

The Committee notes that Manipur has been reeling under an extraordinary crisis for 21 months, with 
hundreds of lives lost and fifty to sixty thousand individuals internally displaced. A significant portion 
of those affected are women and children, who have been rendered homeless, deprived of basic 
necessities, and left in extreme distress. Their access to nutrition, education, and healthcare has been 
severely disrupted. These children, pregnant women, lactating mothers, and elderly women are facing 
immense hardship, leading to grave psychological and social consequences. The absence of economic 
opportunities has further deepened the despair. The Committee notes that the Government has taken 
many steps to support the victims but that more needs to be done. Therefore, the Committee 
recommends that the Ministry of Women and Child Development establish a dedicated special 
committee with a targeted and separate program/policy/scheme for these internally displaced women 
and children. This initiative should ensure direct monitoring and transparent delivery of assistance to 
prevent misuse and guarantee the well- being of affected individuals. Special provisions must be made 
for the education of displaced children, healthcare for lactating mothers, and employment alternatives 
for affected women to rebuild their lives. Steps must be taken to safeguard women and children in relief 
camps from sexual violence.         
(Para 3.4.35 ibid) 
Reply 
Ministry of Women and Child Development is implementing a Centrally Sponsored Scheme namely 
‘Mission Vatsalya’, through the State/ UT Governments on pre-defined cost sharing basis to deliver 
various services for children in difficult circumstances, which include both institutional care and non-
institutional care services. The scheme provides services to the Children in Need of Care and Protection 
(CNCP) as well as Children in Conflict with Law (CCL) for their rehabilitation and social re-integration 
into the mainstream of the society. The Child Care Institutions (CCIs) established under the Mission 
Vatsalya scheme support, inter-alia, age-appropriate education, access to vocational training, recreation, 
health care, counselling etc. Support under non-institutional care is provided by way of sponsorship, 
foster care and after care to children in need of care and protection. Under Non-Institutional Care, 
Rs.4000/- per child is provided. In Manipur, 78 number of CCIs were approved for the State. Child 
Welfare Committees under Sections 27-30 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) 
Act, 2015, are empowered to take decisions with regard to the children in need of care and protection, 
keeping their best interest in mind. They are also mandated to monitor the functioning of the CCIs. The 
JJ Act, 2015 (Section 109) provides for the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights at 
national level and State Commission for Protection of Child Rights at State level respectively to 
monitor the implementation of the Act. Mission Shakti and Mission Poshan 2.0 provide support for 
women and children. Mission Vatsalya envisages State and district level committees for field level 
implementation of the schemes. 
In view of above there may not be requirement to establish a dedicated special committee with 
a targeted and separate program/policy/scheme for these internally displaced women and children.  
The Central Government gives the highest priority to ensuring the safety, security, and empowerment of 
women and has taken several initiatives specially for help and support to the women and children in 
need. Ministry of Women and Child Development (MWCD), under the 15th Finance Commission 
(from FY 2022–23), is implementing three major Centrally Sponsored Schemes for the welfare of 
women and children: 
(i).        Mission Shakti aims at the safety, security, and empowerment of women. 
 It comprises of two verticals: 
a. Sambal vertical focuses on women’s safety and security through components like One Stop 
Centres (OSCs), which provide temporary shelter, medical and police assistance, legal aid, and 
counseling services under one roof, the Women Helpline (181) provides a 24x7 toll-free service to 

52 
 
women seeking support and information. Till 30 June 2025, Manipur had 16 operational OSCs, which 
have assisted 2,059 women and the Women Helpline in the state received 37,882 calls and provided 
assistance to 1,415 women. 
b. Samarthya vertical focuses on women's empowerment. It includes Sakhi Niwas (Working 
Women Hostels) to provide safe and conveniently located accommodation for working women, Shakti 
Sadan is an Integrated Relief and Rehabilitation Home for women in distress situations and difficult 
circumstances, including victims of trafficking, the Hub for Empowerment of Women (HEW) to bridge 
information gaps on women's schemes, and the Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY), 
which provides maternity benefit through Direct Benefit Transfer for the first child (and second child if 
a girl). As on 30.06.2025, 43 Shakti Sadans and 18 Sakhi Niwas are functional in the State of Manipur. 
(ii).        Saksham Anganwadi & Poshan 2.0 aims to improve the nutritional and health status of 
children, pregnant women, and lactating mothers, and also provides early childhood care and education. 
(iii).      Mission Vatsalya focuses on the protection and welfare of children in difficult circumstances, 
including those in need of care and protection and those in conflict with the law. 
In addition to these schemes, several other Ministries of the Central Government are 
implementing welfare programmes that contribute to the overall well-being of women. These include 
Samagra Shiksha, Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalaya, Babu jagjeevan Ram Chhatravas Yojana and

and MUDRA Yojana for access to credit and promotion of women entrepreneurship; and Mahatma 
Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS), Start-up India, and Pradhan

The Committee recommends that additional steps should be taken for provision of nutritious food, 
breakfast, adequate accommodation facility to women and children in relief camps in Manipur. The 
Committee also recommends that Ministry should allocate additional funds for provision of the same as 
well as to facilitate women and children staying in relief camps in Manipur till the situation becomes

Reply 
Ministry of Women and Child Development is implementing a Centrally Sponsored Scheme 
namely ‘Mission Vatsalya’, through the State/ UT Governments on pre-defined cost sharing basis to 
deliver various services for children in difficult circumstances, which include both institutional care and 
non-institutional care services. The scheme provides services to the Children in Need of Care and 
Protection (CNCP) as well as Children in Conflict with Law (CCL) for their rehabilitation and social re-
integration into the mainstream of the society. The Child Care Institutions (CCIs) established under the 
Mission Vatsalya scheme support, inter-alia, age-appropriate education, access to vocational training, 
recreation, health care, counselling etc. Support under non-institutional care is provided by way of 
sponsorship, foster care and after care to children in need of care and protection. Under Non-
Institutional Care, Rs.4000/- per child is provided. In Manipur, 78 number of CCIs were approved for 
the State. 

62 
 
 
Child Welfare Committees under Sections 27-30 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of 
Children) Act, 2015, are empowered to take decisions with regard to the children in need of care and 
protection, keeping their best interest in mind. They are also mandated to monitor the functioning of the 
CCIs. The JJ Act, 2015 (Section 109) provides for the National Commission for Protection of Child 
Rights at national level and State Commission for Protection of Child Rights at State level respectively 
to monitor the implementation of the Act. Mission Shakti and Mission Poshan 2.0 provides support for 
women and children. Mission Vatsalya envisage State and district level committees for field level 
implementation of the schemes.   
 
In view of above there may not be requirement to establish a dedicated special committee with a 
targeted and separate program/policy/scheme for these internally displaced women and children. 
 
Recommendation/Observation by the Committee 
The Committee notes the support being provided to women and children in Manipur 
through existing schemes such as Mission Vatsalya, Mission Shakti and Mission Poshan 2.0. The 
Committee takes note of the institutional and non-institutional care mechanisms available under 
Mission Vatsalya, the approval of 78 Child Care Institutions in the State, and the statutory role of 
Child Welfare Committees and Commissions for Protection of Child Rights in safeguarding the 
interests of children in need of care and protection. 
While acknowledging the framework of schemes and institutional arrangements already 
in place, the Committee observes that the situation in Manipur is of an extraordinary and 
humanitarian nature, involving large numbers of internally displaced women and children 
residing in relief camps for an extended period. The Committee is of the view that reliance solely 
on existing schemes may not be adequate to address the immediate and specific needs particularly 
with regard to provision of nutritious food, breakfast, safe accommodation, health care and 
psycho-social support. Further, the Committee notes that the issue of additional fund allocation to 
relief camps has to be taken care of and, therefore, reiterates that temporary and targeted 
financial support, even within the ambit of existing schemes, is essential to ensure that women and 
children in relief camps are not deprived of the basic facilities. 
The Committee recommends that the Ministry, should undertake a focused assessment of 
the conditions in relief camps in Manipur and consider earmarking additional funds or 
flexibilities under existing schemes to meet emergent needs. Further, the Ministry should ensure 
close monitoring of service delivery on the ground so that women and children continue to receive 
adequate nutrition, shelter and care.   
The Committee recommends the Ministry also coordinate with other Ministries to 
evaluate what measures they may have undertaken to alleviate the issues faced by the Women 
and Children of Manipur.

national level to ensure timely and effective realization of ECCE objectives envisioned under

Recommendation 
The Committee notes that the critical period for fighting malnutrition and stimulating brain 
development is in the first 1,000 days of life, including the time spent in the womb. The Committee notes 
that the current system has institutional care only for children between 3-6 years in Anganwadis for a 
few hours per day. Children between 6 months and 3 years are only provided take-home rations. To 
comprehensively tackle malnutrition, and to enable female labour force participation, the Committee 
endorses the Law Commission’s suggestion that “every child under six should have an unconditional 
right to crèche and day-care…provided by the State.” Accordingly –    
i. All Anganwadis may be converted into full day-care centres (crèches) open for at least 10 
hours for children aged between six months to three years to help all working women and their 
children. As currently provided under the Palna scheme, morning snack, hot cooked meal for lunch, 
and evening snack may be provided to children  
ii.         An additional Anganwadi worker may be hired to care for the children between 6 months and 3 
years in the day care facilities. AWHs may also be considered for the same and redesignated as AWWs. 
          (Para 3.4.64 ibid) 
Reply 
The Ministry of women and Child Development has introduced Palna Scheme under the Samarthya 
Vertical of Umbrella Mission Shakti for all States and UTs w.e.f. 01 April 2022, to provide day care 
facilities and protection to children. 
Anganwadi centres are the world's largest childcare institutions dedicated to providing essential 
care and support to children ensuring delivery of care facilities till the last mile. In a first of its kind 
approach, Ministry has extended the services of childcare through Palna/Anganwadi cum Crèches 
(AWCCs). This will ensure whole day childcare support ensuring their well-being in a safe and secure 
environment. Anganwadi cum Crèche initiative aims to increase ‘women work force participation’ in 
the economy The objective of Palna Scheme is to provide quality crèche facility in safe and secure 
environment for children (from ages 6 months – 6 years), nutritional support, health and cognitive 

64 
 
development of children, growth monitoring &immunization. Crèche facilities under Palna are provided 
to all mothers, irrespective of their employment status. 
The scheme is designed to function in convergence with Anganwadi Services under Saksham 
Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0, thereby ensuring comprehensive early childhood care and nutrition. Each 
Anganwadi-cum-Creche Centre provides evening snacks to enrolled children as part of the Palna 
component. Additionally, morning snacks and hot cooked meal for lunch are provided through the 
Anganwadi platform, ensuring that the children receive supplementary nutrition, health check-ups, 
immunization and growth monitoring in an integrated manner. 
The Palna Scheme provides day-care services for up to 7.5 hours per day, six days a week. As 
per the Standard Operating Procedures and guidelines under Mission Shakti, States and Union 
Territories have the flexibility to determine the operational timings of crèches based on local needs. The 
guidelines mention that “The crèche timings need to be flexible depending on the local requirements. 
Crèches shall be open for 26 days in a month and for seven and half (7-1/2) hours per day as per the 
work schedule of majority of the mothers in the area” and the same can be accessed at 
https://wcd.gov.in/offerings/palna. Each crèches caters up to 25 Children, and offers nutritional support, 
health and cognitive development of children, growth monitoring & immunization. The government has 
made provisions for 2 additional staff per AWCC (one Creche Worker and one Creche Helper), in 
addition to the already existing Anganwadi Worker and Anganwadi Helper. This will also provide 
employment opportunities to women. The State Government is responsible for hiring these honorarium 
workers and helpers. 
 
Recommendation/Observation by the Committee 
 
The Committee examined the reply of the Ministry and appreciates the introduction of 
the Palna Scheme under Mission Shakti and efforts undertaken to extend whole-day childcare 
services for children aged six months to six years, with the objective of improving early childhood 
care, nutrition and enhancing women’s workforce participation. The Committee also notes 
positively the convergence with Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0, provision of supplementary 
nutrition, and the deployment of additional crèche staff at AWCCs. 
However, the Committee is of the view that the current provision of 7.5 hours of day-care

utility of these facilities for mothers of children between six months and three years.

progressively expand AWCCs to all Anganwadi Centres, particularly in urban poor, tribal, and 
high-migration areas.

Recommendation

issues, the initiative focuses on themes like domestic violence, dowry-related disputes, child custody, 
and workplace gender disparities, intending to raise awareness, provide support, and advocate for 
women's rights. 
 Besides Nari Adalat, there are 3 other components under Sambal vertical of Mission Shakti i.e. 
OSC, WHL and BBBP. For implementation of the Sambal vertical of the Mission Shakti, 100% 
financial assistance are provided to States/ UTs. Funds are released to States and UTs on the basis of

are: 
1. Delay in transition to Single Nodal Agency (SNA) in State/UTs and further from SNA to SNA

2. Delay in submission of Utilization Certificate and Statement of Expenditure.

funds under the Nari Adalat scheme vis-à-vis the objectives and scope of the scheme, which aims

on a range of gender-based issues. Further, the Committee notes that the under-utilization of 
funds is primarily due to procedural delays relating to transition to the Single Nodal Agency

of Expenditure, and the fact that the scheme is presently being piloted by  only two States/UTs.

procedural and administrative bottlenecks have resulted in persistently low utilization of funds 
over consecutive years, thereby limiting the outreach and impact of an otherwise important 
initiative. The Committee is of the view that such systemic delays should be addressed in a timely 
manner, particularly given that the scheme is fully funded by the Centre and intended to provide 
accessible justice mechanisms for women at the grassroots level. 
Further, the Committee recommends facilitating faster on boarding of States/UTs, 
providing handholding support for transition to SNA–SPARSH, and streamlining the process for 
submission of Utilization Certificates.

ONE STOP CENTRE 
 
Recommendation

women affected by violence and those in distress. However, the Committee notes that staffs at OSCs are

are very less. Further, they are not being paid salaries on regular basis. Moreover, OSCs are not 
manned as per the population density of respective area/locality. The Committee, therefore, 
recommends that the Ministry should take efforts that OSCs should be manned as per population 
density of respective areas/locality. Further, the Ministry should consider enhancing the salaries of

Adalat. For implementation of the Sambal vertical of the Mission Shakti, 100% financial assistance are

earlier grant and subject to compliance of guidelines of Department of Expenditure prescribed for

Recommendation/Observation by the Committee

and strengthen capacity building of OSC personnel through regional and national training 
programmes, with the involvement of reputed institutions and expert resource persons which 
reflects a positive effort towards improving the quality of service delivery at OSCs. However, the 
Committee observes that several key concerns raised earlier have not been addressed adequately, 
particularly regarding inadequate staffing levels in relation to population density, low 
remuneration of contractual staff, and irregular disbursement of salaries by State Governments. 
The Committee therefore is of the view that training alone may not yield desired outcomes unless 
personnel are adequately compensated, retained, and deployed in sufficient numbers to handle 
the caseload effectively. 
The Committee recommends that the Ministry strengthen monitoring mechanisms and 
engage more closely with States/UTs to ensure that administrative and human resource issues do 
not impede the effective functioning of OSCs and the realization of the scheme’s objectives. 
 
Recommendation 
The Committee observes that One Stop Centers (OSCs) and Women Helplines need sufficient 
integration with law enforcement. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry should take 
the following initiatives: 
(i) AI-Integrated Women’s Helpline: Deploy AI-powered analytics to identify high-risk cases and 
escalate responses to authorities in real time.  
(ii) Expand Mobile One Stop Centers (mOSCs): Introduce mobile OSCs to reach underserved 
areas and provide immediate support for survivors.  
(iii) Integrate Gender Sensitization in Police Training: Make it mandatory for police and judiciary 
officials to undergo regular gender sensitization training. 
(iv) Create Community-Led Safety Networks: Establish women-led neighbourhood watch groups 
trained in self-defence and crisis response.  
The Committee was informed that of the 888 approved OSCs, 802 are currently operational and that 
462 OSCs are integrated with Women Helpline. The Committee recommends the fast-tracking of the 
operationalisation of the remaining OSCs and their integration with WHLs.    
(Para 3.6.11 ibid) 
Reply 
I. With regard to the recommendation of the Committee regarding Deployment of AI-powered 
analytics to identify high-risk cases and escalating responses to authorities in real time, it is submitted 
that the technology solution provider for Women Helpline, C-DAC, has developed application for Call 
operator to digitize the related workflow, and integrate it with the ERSS – 112 nationwide single 
emergency number. Through this, the process of data logging and maintenance has been digitized. 
Further dashboards have been developed at Supervisor, State and National level for monitoring the 
scheme and provide support in evidence and data-based decision making. AI solutions will be explored. 
II. Ministry has made provision for hiring a dedicated vehicle/transport for the OSCs   for the 
purpose of rescuing women in emergency cases and underserved areas.  
III.   Time to time training programmes are being organised for OSC staffs.   

67 
 
IV. Nari Adalats have been set up at the Gram Panchayat level, and all cases of   serious nature 
registered under Nari Adalat must be promptly reported or referred to the respective District One Stop 
Centre (OSC). A detailed Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) outlining the necessary protocols has 
been developed, and the state has been appropriately advised to ensure compliance. 
V. As of now, a total of 960 OSCs have been approved, out of which 820 are operational. 
Regarding integration of the OSCs with the Women Helpline (WHL), it is submitted that 565 OSCs 
have been integrated. Furthermore, as reported by CDAC the required hardware has been delivered to 
675 locations and 602 connectivity to the OSCs has been completed across various States/UTs. 
 
Recommendation/Observation by the Committee 
 
The Committee appreciates the steps taken towards digitization of helpline workflows, 
integration with ERSS–112, development of monitoring dashboards, provision of vehicles for 
emergency response, and the increase in the number of approved and operational OSCs. 
However, the issues such as deployment of AI-powered analytics and mandatory gender 
sensitization training for police and judiciary are not clearly addressed. Further, the Committee 
is of the view that despite progress, a significant number of OSCs remain non-operational and 
many are yet to be fully integrated with Women Helplines and connectivity systems and therefore 
reiterates the need for time-bound operationalisation of all approved OSCs and complete 
integration with WHLs. It further urges the Ministry to adopt advanced technological solutions, 
strengthen coordination with law enforcement agencies, and expedite implementation to ensure 
prompt, effective and survivor-centric support for women in distress. 
 
NARI ADALAT   
 
Recommendation 
The Committee observes that Nari Adalat scheme which aims at empowering women and ensuring 
justice, offers services such as alternate dispute resolution, grievance redressal, counselling, evidence-
based decision-making, pressure group tactics, negotiation, mediation, and reconciliation etc., is very 
slow and its implementation is not up to the mark. Further, this scheme is not operational in every 
district of the country. The Committee, therefore, recommends the Ministry to review the 
implementation of Nari Adalat scheme and also to ensure that each and every district of the country 
should have a Nari Adalat accessible to women. The Committee also recommends that this scheme 
should 106 have support system where counsellors, psychiatrists are attached to it, so that, the 
disadvantage which the women actually face is also addressed.     
(Para 3.6.17 ibid) 
Reply 
Nari Adalat is a component of “Sambal” which is a new component of Mission Shakti of the Ministry 
of Women and Child Development. Nari Adalat scheme provides women with an alternate grievance 
redressal mechanism for resolving cases of harassment, violence and curtailment of rights or 
entitlements at the Gram Panchayat level. The scheme aims to tackle socio-economic and cultural 
challenges faced by women in the area and provides dispute resolution through mediation and referral 
to appropriate institutions such as One Stop Centre, Police Station, District Legal Service Authority and 
Women Help Desk. 
Nari Adalat is being implemented at the Gram Panchayat level. The implementation of the Nari 
Adalat is being done on pilot basis from 2023-24 in selected few States/UTs. The participation of the 
states/UTs is decided in consultation with them. 
The State of Assam and UT of Jammu & Kashmir were selected by the Ministry to implement 
the new component of Nari Adalat on pilot basis. Nari Adalat initiative is being run in 50 Gram 
Panchayats each in the State of Assam and UT of Jammu & Kashmir.  
It is also being piloted and implemented soon in 10 Gram Panchayats each in the state of Bihar, 
Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh and 5 Gram Panchayats of Andaman and Nicobar Islands.  
Further, it is also being piloted in 10 Gram Panchayats of 17 States and 5 Gram Panchayats of 2 
UTs.The Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for Nari Adalat has been reiterated and shared with all 
states and Union Territories. 
 

68 
 
Recommendation/Observation by the Committee 
 
The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry on the implementation of the Nari Adalat 
scheme under Mission Shakti and appreciates the intent of piloting the scheme and the issuance of 
Standard Operating Procedures to States/UTs. The Committee however, observes that the scale 
and pace of implementation remain inadequate in relation to the scheme’s stated objectives. 
Further, the reply does not clearly address the issue of attachment of professional support 
systems such as counsellors and mental health experts, in order to make it accessible to women in 
every district. The Committee therefore, reiterates its earlier recommendation that the Ministry 
should undertake a comprehensive review of the pilot, set clear timelines for phased expansion to 
all districts, and ensure that Nari Adalats are strengthened with counselling and psychological 
support services to effectively address the complex challenges faced by women seeking justice.
